title: Two HD 93683 fits require a companion above 0.25 solar masses under a stated quadrupole model
abstract: We combine the angular momentum needed for a finite change of orbital plane with the largest quadrupole torque. This gives a necessary companion mass without a known outer period. At double-averaged quadrupole order, high outer eccentricity cannot lower this mass floor: its best allowed angular momentum capacity falls as (1-e2^2)^(1/4). For two published HD 93683 point fits, inner masses of 18 and 15 solar masses, and inner eccentricity no larger than the fitted value throughout the interval, the mass floors are 0.2556 and 0.2594 solar masses. We allow either photometric inclination branch and all unknown nodes. The proof needs endpoint change, not a steady drift. These are conditional bounds, not measured masses or new companion detections. They assume the third body supplies the torque alone and do not cover all full Newtonian triples, changing outer eccentricity, stellar-spin torques or extreme inner eccentricity. We include source hashes, code, aggregate inputs, sensitivity tests and a static figure.

display.caption: A companion must pass a lower period from angular momentum capacity and an upper period from torque. High outer eccentricity raises the combined mass floor within the stated quadrupole model.
